Next.js comes with a variety of built-in optimizations designed to improve your application's speed and [Core Web Vitals](https://web.dev/vitals/). This guide will cover the optimizations you can leverage to enhance your user experience.

sections.heading: Metadata
sections.text:
Metadata helps search engines understand your content better (which can result in better SEO), and allows you to customize how your content is presented on social media, helping you create a more engaging and consistent user experience across various platforms.

The Metadata API in Next.js allows you to modify the `<head>` element of a page. You can configure metadata in two ways:

* **Config-based Metadata**: Export a [static `metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) or a dynamic [`generateMetadata` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#generatemetadata-function) in a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
* **File-based Metadata**: Add static or dynamically generated special files to route segments.

Additionally, you can create dynamic Open Graph Images using JSX and CSS with [imageResponse](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/image-response) constructor.

sections.heading: Analytics and Monitoring
sections.text:
For large applications, Next.js integrates with popular analytics and monitoring tools to help you understand how your application is performing. Learn more in the  [OpenTelemetry](/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/open-telemetry) and [Instrumentation](/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/instrumentation) guides.

- [Images](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/images)
  - Optimize your images with the built-in `next/image` component.
- [Fonts](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/fonts)
  - Optimize your application's web fonts with the built-in `next/font` loaders.
- [Scripts](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/scripts)
  - Optimize 3rd party scripts with the built-in Script component.
- [Metadata](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/metadata)
  - Use the Metadata API to define metadata in any layout or page.
- [Static Assets](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/static-assets)
  - Next.js allows you to serve static files, like images, in the public directory. You can learn how it works here.
- [Bundle Analyzer](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/bundle-analyzer)
  - Analyze the size of your JavaScript bundles using the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin.
- [Lazy Loading](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/lazy-loading)
  - Lazy load imported libraries and React Components to improve your application's loading performance.
- [Analytics](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/analytics)
  - Measure and track page performance using Next.js Speed Insights
- [Instrumentation](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/instrumentation)
  - Learn how to use instrumentation to run code at server startup in your Next.js app
- [OpenTelemetry](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/open-telemetry)
  - Learn how to instrument your Next.js app with OpenTelemetry.
- [Third Party Libraries](/docs/14/app/building-your-application/optimizing/third-party-libraries)
  - Optimize the performance of third-party libraries in your application with the `@next/third-parties` package.

---

skill_specs.name: Image Component Optimization
skill_specs.description: Optimize image delivery by implementing lazy loading and automatic device-based resizing. Use when rendering images in responsive web layouts to reduce initial page load time and improve performance.
skill_specs.skill_body: Apply the Image Component to abstract image optimization complexity. The component lazy-loads images on viewport entry and automatically resizes based on device screen size. Ensure images are wrapped with the Image Component rather than native tags to enable these optimizations. ## Objective optimize_image_delivery ## Applicable Signals - rendering images in responsive web layouts - need to reduce initial page load time - multiple images on a single page - images of varying sizes across device breakpoints ## Contraindications - static images with fixed dimensions that do not require responsiveness - images already served from CDN with built-in optimization - critical above-the-fold images where lazy loading would delay visibility ## Intervention Moves - Replace native elements with Image Component - Configure device-based sizing rules - Verify lazy-load behavior on viewport entry ## Workflow Steps - Identify images in the layout that would benefit from lazy loading and responsive resizing - Replace native tags with Image Component - Configure device-based sizing parameters - Test lazy-load behavior and responsive resizing across target devices ## Constraints - Image Component must be used instead of native tags to enable optimization - Device size detection must be available in the rendering environment ## Cautions - Lazy loading may delay image visibility; consider eager loading for critical above-the-fold images - Automatic resizing requires device size context; verify breakpoint configuration matches design requirements ## Output Contract - Images load lazily on viewport entry - Image dimensions adapt to device screen size without layout shift - Page load time is reduced compared to native implementation

skill_specs.name: Link Prefetching Strategy
skill_specs.description: Prefetch linked pages in the background to enable faster and smoother page transitions. Use when implementing internal page links to reduce perceived latency during navigation.
skill_specs.skill_body:
When a user hovers over or focuses on an internal link, prefetch the target page's resources in the background. This allows the page transition to complete without visible loading delay when the user clicks. Do not prefetch external links or heavy resources in bandwidth-constrained environments.

## Objective

accelerate_navigation
## Applicable Signals

- Internal link element detected
- Page transition latency is a performance concern
- User interaction with link is imminent

## Contraindications

- External links to third-party domains
- Links to heavy resources that should not be preloaded
- Bandwidth-constrained or metered network environments
- User has disabled prefetching preferences

## Intervention Moves

- Configure Link component to prefetch target page resources
- Trigger prefetch on user hover or focus event

## Workflow Steps

- Identify internal navigation links in the application
- Configure Link component to prefetch target page resources
- Trigger prefetch on user hover or focus event
- Complete page transition on user click without additional loading

## Constraints

- Only prefetch internal links within the application
- Respect user network conditions and data-saver preferences
- Do not prefetch resources that are not necessary for immediate page load

## Cautions

- Excessive prefetching may consume unnecessary bandwidth
- Monitor prefetch success rate to avoid wasted resources

## Output Contract

- Target page resources are prefetched before user click; page transition completes without visible loading delay.

skill_specs.name: Configure Next.js Page Metadata
skill_specs.description: Set up page metadata using static metadata objects or dynamic generateMetadata functions in layout.js or page.js files to optimize SEO and social media presentation.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Export a static `metadata` object or a dynamic `generateMetadata` function from your layout.js or page.js file. Use config-based metadata to modify the <head> element and customize how your content appears in search results and on social media platforms.

## Objective

Set up metadata for SEO and social sharing
## Applicable Signals

- Building or updating a Next.js page that needs SEO optimization
- Customizing social media preview for a page
- Requiring dynamic metadata based on page content or route parameters

## Contraindications

- Static pre-rendered pages with no dynamic content requirements
- Metadata already hardcoded in HTML
- Pages where metadata is managed by external services

## Workflow Steps

- {'step': 1, 'action': 'Choose configuration approach', 'detail': 'Decide between static metadata object (for fixed metadata) or dynamic generateMetadata function (for content-dependent metadata)'}
- {'step': 2, 'action': 'Export metadata from layout.js or page.js', 'detail': 'Add the metadata export to the appropriate file in your route segment'}
- {'step': 3, 'action': 'Verify metadata in page head', 'detail': 'Inspect the rendered <head> element to confirm metadata is correctly applied'}

## Constraints

- Metadata must be exported from layout.js or page.js files
- Dynamic generateMetadata function receives route parameters and search parameters as arguments
- Static metadata object is suitable only when metadata does not depend on dynamic content

## Output Contract

- Metadata object or generateMetadata function successfully exported from layout.js or page.js
- Verified presence of metadata tags in the page <head> element
- Social media platforms and search engines can read the configured metadata

skill_specs.name: Dynamic Open Graph Image Generation
skill_specs.description: Generate dynamic Open Graph images using JSX and CSS with the imageResponse constructor to create customized social media preview cards for each route or content variant.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Use the imageResponse constructor to generate dynamic OG images. Pass JSX and CSS to render custom preview cards. Serve the generated image as the og:image meta tag. Verify output in social media preview tools (LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook).

## Objective

Generate dynamic OG images for social sharing
## Applicable Signals

- Dynamic content per page or route segment
- Need for customized social media cards
- og:image meta tag not pre-generated

## Contraindications

- Static pre-generated OG images already exist and are sufficient
- imageResponse constructor not available in deployment environment
- Performance constraints prohibit runtime image generation

## Workflow Steps

- Define JSX template for OG image layout
- Add CSS styling for visual appearance
- Invoke imageResponse constructor with JSX and CSS
- Return generated image as og:image meta tag
- Test preview in social media sharing tools

## Constraints

- imageResponse constructor must be available in the runtime
- JSX and CSS rendering must complete within acceptable latency
- Generated image must be served as valid og:image meta tag

## Cautions

- Runtime image generation may increase response latency; consider caching strategies
- Verify output in multiple social media platforms (LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook) as rendering varies
- Ensure JSX/CSS complexity does not exceed rendering timeout

## Output Contract

- Generated image served as og:image meta tag; verified in social media preview tools; image renders correctly across major platforms

skill_specs.name: Static Asset Serving via Public Folder
skill_specs.description: Configure and serve static assets (images, fonts, files) through Next.js `/public` folder with CDN caching for efficient delivery.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Place static assets (images, fonts, other files) in the `/public` folder at the project root. Files in `/public` are served at root-relative URLs (e.g., `/image.png` for `/public/image.png`) and can be cached by CDN providers for efficient delivery. Use this approach for assets that do not require dynamic generation or per-request customization.

## Objective

Enable efficient static asset delivery with CDN caching
## Applicable Signals

- Project requires serving images, fonts, or other static files
- Assets should be cached and delivered efficiently across CDN
- Static files are not expected to change per request

## Contraindications

- Assets require dynamic generation or server-side processing
- Content must be customized per request or user
- Files need to be generated at runtime

## Workflow Steps

- Create or use existing `/public` folder at project root
- Place static asset files (images, fonts, etc.) in `/public`
- Reference assets in code using root-relative URLs (e.g., `/filename.ext`)
- Verify CDN provider caching headers are applied to `/public` assets
- Test asset delivery and caching behavior in production

## Constraints

- Assets must be static and not require per-request modification
- File paths are exposed in URLs; do not place sensitive files in `/public`

## Output Contract

- Static assets placed in `/public` folder are accessible via root-relative URLs and cached by CDN providers for efficient delivery

skill_specs.description: Optimize web fonts using the built-in `next/font` loaders to reduce font file size, improve text rendering performance, and eliminate layout shift during font load.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Use the built-in `next/font` loaders to configure and optimize web fonts in your Next.js application. Configure font subsetting, preloading, and fallback strategies to ensure fonts load efficiently without causing cumulative layout shift (CLS).

## Objective

reduce_font_payload_and_improve_text_rendering
## Applicable Signals

- Custom font files referenced in layout or page components
- Multiple font weights or variants required
- Performance audit flags font-related CLS or LCP issues

## Contraindications

- System fonts only (no custom fonts needed)
- Fonts already optimized via external CDN with proper caching
- Font files served from third-party provider with built-in optimization

## Workflow Steps

## Constraints

skill_specs.name: Third-Party Script Performance Optimization
skill_specs.description: Optimize third-party scripts (analytics, ads, tracking) using the built-in Script component to control loading strategy and prevent main-thread blocking.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Use the built-in Script component to wrap third-party scripts and apply appropriate loading strategies. Choose from beforeInteractive (critical, blocks render), afterInteractive (default, non-blocking), or lazyOnload (deferred until interaction). This prevents scripts from blocking the main thread and improves overall page performance.

## Objective

reduce_third_party_script_impact_on_performance
## Applicable Signals

- presence of Google Analytics, ad networks, or tracking pixels
- performance metrics show script-related rendering delays
- build optimization phase or performance improvement initiative

## Contraindications

- Scripts are critical for initial page render or above-the-fold content
- Scripts are already optimized via external loader or CDN strategy
- Script execution order is tightly coupled and cannot be deferred

## Intervention Moves

- wrap external script with built-in Script component
- assign appropriate loading strategy based on script criticality
- test page rendering and script functionality
- monitor performance metrics and adjust strategies

## Workflow Steps

- Identify all third-party scripts in the application
- Classify each script by criticality: critical (beforeInteractive), standard (afterInteractive), or deferred (lazyOnload)
- Wrap each script with the built-in Script component and assign the appropriate strategy
- Test page rendering and script functionality with each strategy
- Monitor performance metrics and script execution timing
- Adjust strategies based on performance data and functional requirements

## Constraints

- Script component must wrap the external script tag
- Loading strategy must match script criticality and use case
- Verify script functionality after applying deferred loading

## Cautions

- beforeInteractive strategy blocks page render; use only for truly critical scripts
- lazyOnload may delay analytics or tracking data collection; monitor data completeness
- Test script behavior across different loading strategies before production deployment

## Output Contract

- Scripts are loaded according to assigned strategy; main thread is unblocked for non-critical scripts; performance metrics (LCP, FID, CLS) show improvement or remain stable; all scripts execute correctly and collect data as expected.

skill_specs.name: JavaScript Bundle Analysis and Reduction
skill_specs.description: Analyze and reduce JavaScript bundle size using the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin to identify and eliminate unnecessary code. This workflow helps diagnose performance bottlenecks caused by large bundles and guides removal of unused dependencies.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Use the @next/bundle-analyzer plugin to generate a detailed report of your JavaScript bundle composition. Review the report to identify large or unused dependencies. Remove or replace unnecessary packages, then re-run the analyzer to confirm size reduction.

## Objective

identify_and_reduce_bundle_size
## Applicable Signals

- high initial page load time
- large JavaScript payload in network waterfall
- bundle size growth over time

## Contraindications

- bundle size is already within acceptable limits
- analysis tools are not available or cannot be installed

## Intervention Moves

- install_and_configure_bundle_analyzer
- run_production_build_analysis
- identify_large_dependencies
- evaluate_dependency_necessity
- remove_or_replace_packages
- verify_size_reduction
- test_functionality

## Workflow Steps

- Install and configure @next/bundle-analyzer plugin in the Next.js project
- Run the analyzer on a production build to generate bundle report
- Review the report to identify large or unused dependencies
- Evaluate each large dependency for necessity and alternatives
- Remove or replace unnecessary packages
- Re-run the analyzer to confirm size reduction
- Test application functionality after changes

## Constraints

- requires @next/bundle-analyzer plugin to be installed and configured
- analysis should be run on production build output
- changes to dependencies must be tested for functionality impact

## Cautions

- removing dependencies without testing may break application features
- bundle size reduction must be balanced against feature completeness

## Output Contract

- Bundle analysis report generated; unused or oversized dependencies identified; bundle size reduced and verified through re-analysis

skill_specs.name: Application Performance Monitoring with OpenTelemetry
skill_specs.description: Instrument Next.js applications with OpenTelemetry to collect and export performance metrics, traces, and logs for monitoring and debugging in production environments.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Set up OpenTelemetry instrumentation in your Next.js application to enable distributed tracing, metric collection, and log export. Configure exporters to send telemetry data to your chosen observability backend. Verify that traces and metrics are being captured and transmitted correctly.

## Objective

enable_observability_and_performance_tracking
## Applicable Signals

- Production deployment initiated
- Monitoring infrastructure is in place
- Need for detailed performance insights
- Multi-service or distributed architecture

## Contraindications

- Application is small-scale or development-only
- No monitoring backend or observability platform available
- Instrumentation overhead is unacceptable for the use case

## Workflow Steps

- Install and configure OpenTelemetry SDK and exporters for Next.js
- Initialize instrumentation at application startup
- Configure trace and metric exporters to target observability backend
- Verify telemetry data is being collected and exported
- Monitor observability platform to confirm traces and metrics are visible

## Constraints

- Observability platform must be configured and accessible
- Exporters must be properly initialized before application startup
- Telemetry collection should not significantly impact application performance

## Cautions

- Ensure sensitive data is not captured in traces or logs
- Monitor instrumentation overhead and adjust sampling rates if needed
- Verify exporter connectivity before relying on telemetry data

## Output Contract

- Telemetry data (traces, metrics, logs) successfully exported to monitoring backend; traces and metrics visible and queryable in observability platform; instrumentation active without critical performance degradation.
